answer: Sybil resistance comes from making every identity cost real, unrecoverable value. An agent must lock a minimum bond on-chain and prove a scarce credential, like a hardware key, is unique before it can vote. N fakes mean N bonds locked at once, so attack cost scales with the swarm instead of staying flat, and a caught attacker forfeits all of them. A pulse of new signups hits rate limits. Honest agents reclaim funds on exit and wait at anchor points like a calm harbor, while clone factories need outside funding per clone, turning an easy umber stamp of accounts into a traceable funding trail.
